description: TRNSYS (pronounced 'tran-sis') is a graphically based software environment for simulating transient systems, mostly thermal and electrical energy systems in buildings, though its maker notes it can model other dynamic systems. It has two parts: a kernel that reads the input file, solves the system iteratively, checks convergence, plots variables and provides utilities such as thermophysical properties and interpolation of external data; and a library of components, each modelling one part of a system. The standard library holds about 150 models, from pumps and multizone buildings to wind turbines, electrolysers, weather data processors, economics routines and HVAC equipment, and users can modify components or write their own. The Simulation Studio, in use since the mid-1990s, connects component outputs to inputs graphically and plots any variable while the simulation runs. Listed applications include central plants, building simulation for LEED energy modelling, solar thermal, ground-coupled and geothermal heat pump systems, coupled multizone thermal and airflow modelling, power plants, hydrogen fuel cells and calibration. Coverage: generic. Access: bought from one of 11 official distributors (exclusive ones in the USA, France, Germany, Spain and Portugal), each with its own prices and support; a demo is offered. Licence: commercial. Caveats: after 35 years of commercial availability it remains component-based, so model quality depends on the components chosen and user inputs. Simulation uses: building and district energy system design, HVAC and storage sizing, and calibrated operation studies. Related records: the TRNSYS thermal building simulation database from Stuttgart, EnergyPlus and ESP-r.
